Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 63, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Munafiqun (The Hypocrites)

It is Medinan according to the consensus. And Allah knows best.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah."﴾ The people of tafsir (ahl al-tafsir) said: The surah was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his companions. They would come to the Prophet and say: "We believe in you, and we bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah, and that what you have brought is true." Then, when they returned to those among whom they were, they manifested disbelief. It is also related from some of them that His saying, exalted is He, "bear witness" (nashhadu), means "swear" (nahlifu), as evidenced by the fact that Allah, exalted is He, said after this verse: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾.

The poet said:

(And I call Allah to witness that I love her... so this is for her from me, and what she has for me is not)

That is: I swear.

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars﴾, it is a consolation of the heart of the Prophet and a comfort to him. Its meaning: my knowledge that you are the Messenger of Allah, and my testimony to you of that, is better than their testimony.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, they are liars﴾, Abu Ubayd said: That is, the disbelievers; he names disbelief by the name of lying. Another said: It is lying in its literal sense. Their statement was called a lie because they lied to their own hearts. It was also said: when they manifested with their tongues something contrary to what was in their inner selves, it was called lying, like a man who reports a thing contrary to how it actually is.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 63, verse 2:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾, meaning: a cover for what they concealed of disbelief. It was also said: "a shield," meaning they use them as a protection against being killed, like the (mijann) shield with which a fighter takes cover from the weapon of the enemy.

His saying: ﴿and they hinder (others) from the way of God﴾, meaning: they prevented people from the path of faith. The meaning of their hindering people from the way of God is that they used to say to the weak among the Muslims: "We bear witness in the presence of this man and display the opposite of what we conceal. If he were a prophet, he would know our secret," and they prevented them from associating with his companions.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, what they used to do is evil﴾, meaning: evil is their deed. It is recited in the irregular (shadhdh) reading: "They have taken their faith as a shield," with a kasra on the alif, whereas the well-known reading is īmānahum with a fatḥa, meaning "their oaths," the plural of yamīn (oath).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 63, verse 3:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is because they believed, then they disbelieved﴾, meaning: they believed with their tongues, and disbelieved with their hearts.

And His saying: ﴿So their hearts were sealed﴾, meaning: their hearts were sealed up, so faith and the acceptance of the truth do not enter them.

And His saying: ﴿So they do not understand﴾, meaning: they do not reflect upon (lit. contemplate, tadabbur) [the matter]. Fiqh (understanding, comprehension) is contemplation and grasping. It is also said: ﴿So they do not understand﴾ means they do not reason (ya'qilun), as though they did not accept the religion despite the clear evidences for it, placing them in the position of those who do not reason.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 63, verse 4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when you see them, their bodies please you﴾. In the exegesis: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul was a man who was large-bodied, eloquent, handsome, and sharp-tongued. Al-Zajjaj said: God, exalted is He, informed that their bodies were sound, their appearance pleasing, and their tongues eloquent. This is in His saying: ﴿And if they speak, you listen to what they say﴾, meaning, to the tongue they possess. Then He said concerning them: ﴿As if they were propped-up pieces of wood﴾, meaning: they are figures without substance, forms without meanings. They were likened to wood because wood has no heart and no intellect, and it neither comprehends news nor understands it. It is said in common usage: "So-and-so is wood," meaning he has no intellect and no understanding. It was also recited as "khashab" with a sukun on the shin, and both have the same meaning. It is said: badan and badanah, thamar and thamarah. So "khashab" and "khashab" are plural, and the singular is "khashabah," and its example is what we have mentioned.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿propped-up﴾, meaning: leaning against the wall. ʿAli ibn ʿIsa said: He made them like rotten timbers, eaten away within, sound in appearance.

His saying: ﴿They think every cry is against them﴾, meaning: whenever they hear a call or hear someone reciting a lost item or any sound whatsoever, they think that they are the intended target of that sound, and that their inner secrets have been exposed to the Muslims. This is a description of their cowardice and fear of the Muslims. Some exegetes said its meaning is that whenever the Prophet mentioned something, they thought it concerned their affair and their situation. It was also said: whenever a verse or a surah was revealed, out of fear they thought it had been revealed about them; this was related by Ibn Jurayj. And they recited for Jarir on cowardice:

(You kept thinking every thing after them was cavalry charging against them, and men.)

And another said:

(I became so frightened that if a dust-mote passed by, I would say: an enemy and a vanguard of a company.)

His saying: ﴿They are the enemy﴾, meaning: the enemies.

His saying: ﴿So beware of them﴾. He said this because they convey the secrets of the Muslims to the polytheists and make the weak among the Muslims cowardly.

His saying: ﴿May God fight them﴾, meaning: may He disgrace and destroy them. It was also said: He placed them in the position of one who is fought by a dominant enemy.

His saying: ﴿How are they turned away?﴾, meaning: how are they diverted from the truth despite its manifestness? This includes condemnation of their conduct and expressing amazement at them on the part of the Messenger of God.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 63, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you"﴾. The believers used to say to the hypocrites: "Come to the Prophet, acknowledge your sins, and he will ask forgiveness for you." They would shake their heads and look to the right and left, mocking. It was said: this was specifically concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. Some of the Companions said this to him, so he twisted his head and shook it in mockery. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿they turn their heads aside﴾. It is also read with the light (takhfif) pronunciation. Its meaning: they twisted their heads. Whoever reads with the heavy (tashdid) pronunciation, it is for emphasis.

And His saying: ﴿and you see them turning away while they are arrogant﴾, meaning: they turn away, refusing to accept faith.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 63, verse 6:

And His saying: ﴿It is the same for them whether you seek forgiveness for them or do not seek forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them.﴾ Its meaning is that your seeking forgiveness for them does not benefit them, and that their presence and their absence are alike (in the sight of Allah). If it is asked: How could the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) seek forgiveness for them when he knew that they were hypocrites? The answer is: he used to seek forgiveness for them because they would come seeking forgiveness and asking him for pardon and pardoning, as we mentioned in Surat al-Tawbah, but it did not benefit them, because they were disbelievers in the sight of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾, that is, the hypocrites, who are disbelievers, defiantly disobedient, and hypocrites. Some of them related from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman that he was asked: "Who is the hypocrite?" He said: "The one who describes faith but does not act upon it." And from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: "I do not fear for you a believer whose faith is evident, nor a disbeliever whose disbelief is evident; rather, I fear for you every hypocrite who is eloquent of tongue."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 63, verse 7:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah, until they disperse."﴾ It is read in the irregular (shadhdh) reading, "until they disperse" (hatta yanfadu), from al-nafd, meaning: until they empty their containers, so that they become poor and scatter.

As for His saying, ﴿They are the ones who say﴾, it is said that the waw (and) is omitted, and its meaning is: "And they are the ones who say." Likewise in His saying, ﴿If we return to Medina﴾, meaning: "And they say." The poet said: "For some matter the nights have turned, / For some matter the stars have moved."

That is: "And for some matter."

As for His saying, ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah﴾, the verse was revealed on a specific occasion, which is what al-Zuhri related from 'Urwa, from Usama ibn Zayd, that 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, had hired a man from Ghifar called Jahjaha to work for him in some of the campaigns, namely the Battle of al-Muraysi'. A dispute arose between him and a man from the Ansar over the top of a well for drawing water. The Ansari cried, "O Ansar!" and Jahjaha cried, "O Muhajirun!" The Prophet heard this and said: "What is this, the calls of the Jahiliyya? Leave them, for they are foul." This reached 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and he became angry and said: "This is like the saying of the first one: 'Fatten your dog and it will devour you.'" He also said: "Indeed, if you had obeyed me, you would not have spent on those who have gathered around this man." The Ansar used to spend on the Muhajirun, and they would disperse from him. He also said: "If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it," meaning by "the mightier" himself and by "the meaner" Muhammad. This reached the Prophet, and 'Umar said: "Let me strike the neck of this hypocrite." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Let not people say that Muhammad kills his companions." That is: "I will not kill him for this."

He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Abu 'Ali al-Shafi'i informed us of this in Mecca; Abu al-Hasan ibn Faras informed us; Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Dibli informed us; Abu 'Abd Allah Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi informed us; Sufyan informed us, from al-Zuhri... the hadith.

Al-Bukhari also mentioned this report in his book, through the narration of Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "I was with 'Umar on a campaign, and I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul say to his companions: 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse.' He also said: 'If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it.' So I came to 'Umar and mentioned that to him, and 'Umar mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah. Then Ibn Ubayy came to the Prophet and swore that he had not said it, so he (the Prophet) believed him and called me a liar. I was overcome with a grief such as I had never experienced before, until I sat in my house. Then Allah, Exalted, revealed this verse and the one before it. The Messenger of Allah called me and said: 'Indeed Allah, Exalted, has confirmed you.'"

In the narration of Sufyan, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir: "A man from the Muhajirun struck a man from the Ansar, so the Ansari cried, 'O Ansar!' and the Muhajiri cried, 'O Muhajirun!' The Ansar were more numerous than the Muhajirun when the Messenger of Allah came to Medina, but the Muhajirun later increased. When 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul heard that, he said what we have mentioned," and he related the hadith, close to what we mentioned at first. He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Abu 'Ali al-Shafi'i informed us of this in Mecca, with the chain of narration we mentioned from Sufyan.

As for His saying, ﴿until they disperse﴾, that means: until they scatter.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth﴾, its meaning: if you do not spend, still to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, and He provides for you. It is said: the treasures of the heavens are the rain, and the treasures of the earth are the plants. And it is reported from some of them: the treasures of the heavens are what He decrees, and the treasures of the earth are what He gives. And some of the masters of inner insight said: the treasures of the heavens are the unseen matters, and the treasures of the earth are the hearts. The correct view is the first.

His saying: ﴿But the hypocrites do not understand﴾ has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 63, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They say, "If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more contemptible."﴾ We have already mentioned it. Al-a'azz (the more honorable) is the one more able to prevent others, and al-adhall (the more contemptible) is the one more incapable of benefiting others. It has also been said that its meaning is: "The mighty will surely expel the humiliated therefrom." Regarding af'al in the sense of fa'il, al-Farazdaq said:

(Indeed He who raised the sky built for us ... a house whose pillars are more lofty and taller.) That is: a lofty, tall house.

And His saying: ﴿But to Allah belongs honor, and to His Messenger and to the believers﴾, that is: dominance, protection and strength. Honor belongs to Allah by virtue of His honor in His essence, and honor belongs to His Messenger and to the believers by virtue of what Allah, exalted is He, has granted them of dominance, protection and strength.

And His saying: ﴿But the hypocrites do not know﴾, that is: they do not know that honor and dominance belong to Allah, to His Messenger and to the believers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 63, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah﴾. That is: let them not preoccupy you. Its meaning: do not busy yourselves with looking after your wealth and your children, for that would distract you from the remembrance of Allah, as it distracted the hypocrites. The remembrance of Allah here is belief in Him.

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever does that, those are the losers﴾. That is: those who are cheated out of their shares. It is also said: they are those who cheated themselves and lost them in the Hereafter. It is narrated from ʿAṭāʾ that the remembrance of Allah here refers to the five daily prayers. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it is everything that Allah has made obligatory.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 63, verse 10:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And spend of what We have provided you﴾. The more correct view is that it refers to zakat (obligatory alms). It was also said that it is voluntary charity (sadaqah al-tatawwu'), and everything Allah the Exalted has urged spending on in good causes.

His words: ﴿before death comes to one of you, and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me﴾, meaning: "Why will You not delay me?"

His words: ﴿for a brief term﴾, meaning: for a short period. Ibn 'Abbas said: Everyone who has wealth and does not pay its zakat will ask Allah for a return (to the world) when death is present to him. They said to him, "O Ibn 'Abbas, fear Allah, for the return is only for the disbeliever." He said, "Recite this verse: ﴿And spend of what We have provided you﴾ up to the end of the verse." In another narration: this applies to the Hajj instead of zakat.

His words: ﴿and I would be among the righteous﴾. It is read "wa-akun" (and I would be). Whoever reads "wa-akun" then it is conjoined to His words "fa-asaddaq" (so I would give charity). It was said to Ibn 'Umar: "How did you differ from the Mushaf in His words ﴿and I would be among the righteous﴾?" He said: "It is like their saying in the abjad spelling, kalaman, and it is kalamun." 

As for the explanation of the verse according to the reading without the waw: "And if You delay me, I would give charity and I would be among the righteous." It was also said: "asaddaq" means "azakki" (I would pay zakat), and "akun min al-salihin" means "ahuddu" (I would perform Hajj).

"The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah will never delay a soul when its term has come.﴾ That is: it neither comes forward nor is put back when the appointed time arrives.

And His words: ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.﴾ The meaning is clear."
